claims.text: Aurora says 20+ driverless trucks are already built and coming into its fleet, and that production is accelerating.
claims.quote: We have 20+ driverless trucks already built and coming into the fleet, and production is accelerating.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says the Aurora Driver passed 500,000 commercial driverless miles in September and has kept 100% on-time delivery since launch.
claims.quote: in September the Aurora Driver surpassed 500,000 commercial driverless miles, maintaining 100% on-time delivery, since launch.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says Charger Logistics selected it under an MOU to own and operate 500 trucks through Aurora's DaaS business model.
claims.quote: Charger Logistics has selected Aurora to scale their autonomous fleet with an MOU to own and operate 500 trucks through our DaaS business model
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says Charger expects truck delivery in 2027 and 2028 and plans to start between Dallas and Laredo. The letter calls that one of Charger's busiest freight routes in the Sun Belt.
claims.quote: With truck delivery expected in 2027 and 2028, Charger plans to use the Aurora Driver to add capacity on its network and drive higher utilization, starting between Dallas and Laredo, one of its busiest freight routes in the Sun Belt.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: The letter quotes Andy Khera, president of Charger Logistics, saying autonomous operations on the Laredo corridor brought immediate operational benefits.
claims.quote: Since launching autonomous operations along the Laredo corridor, we’ve realized immediate operational benefits that point to a clear path to scaling.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says that in November the Aurora Driver will run directly to sites for several driverless customers, including automated navigation through security checkpoints.
claims.quote: In November, the Aurora Driver will be operating directly to sites for several driverless customers, including automated navigation through security checkpoints.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says it will begin site-to-site driverless operations for the majority of its customers over the coming months.
claims.quote: Over the coming months, we will begin site-to-site driverless operations for the majority of our customers.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: The letter says autonomous trucks have historically relied on voluntary enhanced pre-trip inspections to bypass weigh stations.
claims.quote: Historically, autonomous trucks have relied on voluntary enhanced pre-trip inspections (EPTI) to bypass weigh stations.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says the Aurora Driver can now determine on its own whether a weigh station is open, navigate to an available scale lane and adapt to different scale configurations.
claims.quote: With our weigh station traversal capability, the Aurora Driver can now autonomously determine if a station is open, navigate to an available scale lane, and adapt to different scale configurations.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says its initial production ramp over the past month was held back by material availability, component quality and problems found in end-of-line testing.
claims.quote: While our initial ramp volume over the past month was constrained by material availability, component quality, and issues identified during end-of-line testing, our team moved quickly to address these pre-production bottlenecks.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says it now expects to reach its targeted production rate of 20 trucks per week in early December.
claims.quote: we now expect to achieve our targeted production rate of 20 trucks per week in early December.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says its production ramp is about six weeks behind its prior plan and it now expects 2026 revenue of approximately $9 million.
claims.quote: Reflecting a production ramp about six weeks behind our prior plan, we now expect 2026 revenue of approximately $9 million
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora reported third quarter 2026 revenue of $3 million from driverless and vehicle operator-supervised commercial loads.
claims.quote: Third quarter 2026 revenue totaled $3 million across driverless and vehicle operator-supervised commercial loads.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora reported a third quarter operating loss of $257 million, a figure that includes stock-based compensation.
claims.quote: Third quarter operating loss, including stock-based compensation (SBC), totaled $257 million.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says it expects to pass the 200-truck milestone by the end of February.
claims.quote: We anticipate exceeding the 200-truck milestone by the end of February.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says it remains on track to end 2027 with more than 1,000 driverless trucks in operation.
claims.quote: we remain on track to exit 2027 with more than 1,000 driverless trucks in operation.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says AUMOVIO has begun design validation of Aurora's third-generation commercial hardware kit and is finalizing the line concept and production flow at its dedicated facility in New Braunfels, Texas.
claims.quote: AUMOVIO has initiated design validation for our third-generation commercial hardware kit, while finalizing the line concept and production flow at its dedicated facility in New Braunfels, Texas.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora says initial line bring-up remains on track for later this year, ahead of a planned start of production in the second half of 2027.
claims.quote: Initial line bring-up remains on track for later this year ahead of planned start of production in the second half of 2027.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: The letter says Charger Logistics' intent to own and operate 500 trucks reflects current plans and discussions under a non-binding MOU.
claims.quote: Statements in this investor letter about Charger Logistics’ intent to own and operate 500 Aurora Driver-powered trucks reflect current plans and discussions, as reflected in the non-binding MOU
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: Aurora's letter says FMCSA granted Aurora and the industry a five-year exemption. It lets driverless trucks use cab-mounted warning beacons in place of manually placed roadside warning devices when a truck is stopped.
claims.quote: Earlier this month, FMCSA granted Aurora and the industry an important, five-year exemption, permitting driverless trucks to use cab-mounted warning beacons in place of traditional, manually-placed roadside warning devices when a commercial motor vehicle is stopped.
claims.document: Aurora Innovation, Third Quarter 2026 Shareholder Letter (Exhibit 99.1)

claims.text: In a September 23rd, 2026 release Aurora described a Dallas-to-Houston commercial route of its own and said it was offering driverless passenger rides on a segment of it.
claims.quote: Company offers industry-first driverless passenger rides on a segment of its Dallas-to-Houston commercial route
claims.document: Aurora Outlines 2030 Vision to Scale to 30,000 Driverless Trucks at Analyst and Investor Day

claims.text: San Antonio Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones issued a statement on October 29th, 2026 after City Council passed a new process for considering data centers in the city.
claims.quote: Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones released the following statement on City Council passing a new process for data center consideration in San Antonio.
claims.document: Mayor’s Statement on Council Decision on Data Centers

claims.text: Mayor Jones said the council action ensures City Council can review each data center application, which she called an important safeguard given how quickly the industry is changing.
claims.quote: Today, we took a step forward to ensure City Council has the opportunity to review each data center application, and that is an important safeguard given how quickly this industry is changing.
claims.document: Mayor’s Statement on Council Decision on Data Centers

claims.text: Mayor Jones said her own provisions on transparency, public health and property values were left out of the council resolution. She said they will serve as her office's standards when each application is reviewed.
claims.quote: While my provisions focused on increasing transparency, protecting public health, and protecting property values were not included in today’s resolution, they will serve as my office’s standards when each data center application is reviewed.
claims.document: Mayor’s Statement on Council Decision on Data Centers

claims.text: Texas Public Radio reported that San Antonio council members approved the new data center policy in a 9 to 2 vote on Thursday.
claims.quote: Council members approved the new policy in a 9-2 vote on Thursday.
claims.document: San Antonio leaders will now have to OK every new data center

claims.text: Texas Public Radio reported that the new rules allow approved data centers only in commercial or industrial zones.
claims.quote: The new rules will only allow the approved data centers in commercial or industrial zones.
claims.document: San Antonio leaders will now have to OK every new data center

claims.text: Texas Public Radio reported that council members Misty Spears of District 9 and Marc Whyte of District 10 voted against the policy.
claims.quote: Council members Misty Spears (D9) and Marc Whyte (D10) both voted no.
claims.document: San Antonio leaders will now have to OK every new data center

rejected.reason: No primary Aurora page fetched on November 3rd names it. Only Dallas to Houston appears as a current Aurora route (c21).

rejected.finding: The letter's Dallas and Laredo mention as a current Aurora route
rejected.reason: The letter says Charger plans to start between Dallas and Laredo with trucks expected in 2027 and 2028. Kept in c4 in future tense only.

rejected.finding: Public Citizen's count of TCEQ data center permits after the September 21st pause
rejected.reason: Journalism only, and the count's own PDF is an image file. Not used.
